text: Article · research post · rohanbansal.com Training a 4B model to produce 81% faster query plans than Postgres Rohan Bansal (independent; written at the Recurse Center) · published 16 September 2026 In one line: On the 113 queries of the IMDb Join Order Benchmark, a 4B open model post-trained by one person for about $1,200 (LoRA SFT on about 400 GPT-6 Astra agent trajectories, then RL with a noise-aware reward) writes pg_hint_plan hints whose plans average 1.40x the speed of Postgres 18's own in one search (geometric mean); the headline 1.81x, or 44.7% less summed time, is the best of three searches picked by single timings, with the search time excluded and the planner at its default cost settings.
